rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly with no ICE fallback, so this round pushes obfuscation strength up moderately across the board. SUB and BCF get the highest SecurityGain weights because this benchmark is dominated by small, arithmetic-heavy template functions (test_constant instantiations) and a very large main — constant-folding-friendly code is cheap to obfuscate with instruction substitution and benefits most from bogus control flow, and the small function bodies keep BCF's size bloat proportional. FLA is raised next since nested loops in stepanov_vector/loop_unroll tolerate flattening well. IBR and ICALL are given solid weights to add inter-procedural and call-site indirection on the many template instantiations, diversifying the transformation mix. SPLIT stays moderate: it mostly adds size, so its SizeCost weight is the highest of any pass to keep it targeted at the few large functions (main) rather than the long tail of tiny templates. IGV remains the lightest transform — global-variable encryption has limited payoff for this compute-bound workload and carries correctness risk on the benchmark's shared test harness state. RuntimeCost and SizeCost weights are kept in the mid range everywhere so hot-loop functions (stepanov_abstraction, loop_unroll) naturally shed the more expensive passes, preserving acceptable runtime while still layering SUB+FLA+IBR as a defense-in-depth combination on cold code.
